article_title: An immersive mixed reality surgical self-training system for precise pedicle screw placement: a randomized controlled trial.
citation: Qian He, Jiahao Li, Ye Xiao, Jingjing Tian, Ningbo Mao, Sheng Lu, Yu Zhang, Yu Zhao. (2025). An immersive mixed reality surgical self-training system for precise pedicle screw placement: a randomized controlled trial. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07978-y
title: IMR-SS: an immersive mixed reality surgical self-training system combining holographic guidance with a physical spine phantom
description: IMR-SS is a self-training platform for pedicle screw placement that "combines holographic real-time training instructions with a physical spine phantom to integrate virtual simulation with hands-on training." It comprises three modules — Teaching, Hands-on, and Assessment — implemented on HoloLens 2 with Unity and MRTK, using a patient-specific 3D-printed lumbar phantom (L1–L5), real tracked surgical instruments feeding 6-DoF poses to a digital twin, and real-time precision and safety metrics that trigger on-device warnings and adaptive guidance. A browser-based demo is provided in the supplementary material.
requirements: A HoloLens 2 headset, a standard PC, two tracking cameras, and patient-specific 3D-printed vertebral models; expert-validated curriculum content and expert-defined assessment thresholds
constraints: Evaluated only for pedicle screw placement with novice undergraduates in short-term training; no cadaver or operating-room transfer studies; soft-tissue handling and non-technical skills not evaluated
target_learners: novice undergraduate medical students learning spine surgery basics
target_learning_goals: psychomotor skill of pedicle screw placement
procedural knowledge of the pedicle screwing workflow
examples: In the trial, the IMR group learned with IMR-SS through timed instrument preview, model preview, and procedure instructions, then practiced one screw insertion into L3 with real-time holographic guidance before an unaided assessment
key_sources: Qian He, Jiahao Li, Ye Xiao, Jingjing Tian, Ningbo Mao, Sheng Lu, Yu Zhang, Yu Zhao. (2025). An immersive mixed reality surgical self-training system for precise pedicle screw placement: a randomized controlled trial. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07978-y

article_title: An immersive mixed reality surgical self-training system for precise pedicle screw placement: a randomized controlled trial.
citation: Qian He, Jiahao Li, Ye Xiao, Jingjing Tian, Ningbo Mao, Sheng Lu, Yu Zhang, Yu Zhao. (2025). An immersive mixed reality surgical self-training system for precise pedicle screw placement: a randomized controlled trial. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07978-y
title: Modular IMR-SS training framework integrating teaching, hands-on practice, and assessment phases
description: The authors propose a modular curriculum framework for immersive mixed reality surgical self-training that "tightly integrates teaching, hands-on, and assessment phases, effectively bridging the gap between virtual simulation and physical practice." Guided by the Cognitive Affective Model of Immersive Learning, the teaching module follows a Preparation–Exploration–Exercise–Reflection cycle with the procedure decomposed via expert-led cognitive task analysis; the hands-on module pairs patient-specific 3D-printed models with holographic digital twins; the assessment module tracks process errors and breaches, not just final outcomes, and closes the loop with real-time multimodal feedback. The authors argue this structure may explain performance benefits where less structured MR training attempts did not.
requirements: A theory-driven, expert-validated curriculum; expert-defined accuracy and safety thresholds; spatial tracking of instruments and phantom to synchronize virtual and physical contexts
constraints: Demonstrated for one classic spine procedure; the authors state future work must develop IMR-SSs for more complex surgeries and validate generalizability across procedures
target_learners: novice medical students in surgical skills training
target_learning_goals: surgical procedural skill acquisition
safe and accurate instrument handling
examples: The trial operationalized the framework with four sessions: interaction learning, learning, exercise on a physical phantom, and unassisted assessment, with identical content and timing across groups

article_title: Mental health mediates the association between cardiorespiratory fitness and academic performance in European schoolchildren.
citation: Muntaner-Mas Adrià, Valenzuela Pedro L., Pinto-Escalona Tania, Erickson Kirk I., Martínez-de-Quel Óscar. (2025). Mental health mediates the association between cardiorespiratory fitness and academic performance in European schoolchildren. Jornal de Pediatria. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jped.2024.10.013
title: Improving children's cardiorespiratory fitness may be targeted to reduce mental health difficulties with potential benefits on academic performance
description: The article proposes that CRF is a modifiable factor that interventions can target: "the present results are of potential relevance given that CRF is a modifiable factor that could be a target outcome to be included in interventions aiming to improve academic performance and mental health in children." The conclusion suggests "enhancing CRF during childhood may contribute to better academic performance, partially via improvements in mental health," particularly for children with mental health difficulties and low CRF levels.
requirements: Interventions should aim to improve CRF, e.g., through physical activity or physical exercise, which the article calls arguably the most effective intervention for the improvement of CRF.
constraints: The supporting evidence is cross-sectional, so the statistical mediation results should be interpreted in this context and longitudinal studies are warranted.
target_learners: children aged 7–8 years in primary school
target_learning_goals: academic performance across school subjects
mental health / psychosocial functioning
examples: The study analyzed baseline data from a multi-country cluster randomized controlled trial of a school-based karate intervention, using CRF, SDQ mental health and teacher grades from 507 children in five European countries.

citation: Mazur L, Butler L, Mitchell C, Lashani S, Buchanan S, Fenison C, Adapa K, Tan X, An S, Ra J. (2025). Effect of Immersive Virtual Reality Teamwork Training on Safety Behaviors During Surgical Cases: Nonrandomized Intervention Versus Controlled Pilot Study. JMIR Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.2196/66186
title: 45-minute immersive VR training based on TeamSTEPPS principles with pre- and postdebriefing
description: The intervention is a 45-minute immersive VR-based training delivered via a head-mounted display (Pico Neo 3 Pro Eye with 6DoF), built from 360° filmed scenes of a surgical error whose contributing factors are explained by the Swiss Cheese Model and HFACS. As the article states, "Participants were exposed to a 45-minute immersive VR-based training based on TeamSTEPPS principles to improve safety behaviors." Training included a standardized pre- and postbriefing grounded in TeamSTEPPS principles, in which participants interpreted the TENTS- and HFACS-related factors behind the depicted patient safety incident.
requirements: A VR head-mounted display and 360° filmed scenarios of a realistic surgical error with actors who have lived health care experience
constraints: Evaluated only as a pilot in a single academic medical center with 10 intervention surgeons
target_learners: surgeons (attendings and residents) in operating room settings
target_learning_goals: TeamSTEPPS-related safety behaviors including communication, leadership, situation monitoring, and mutual support
examples: The training was delivered to 10 volunteer surgeons using the Pico Neo 3 Pro Eye headset, with debriefing data analyzed phenomenologically

article_title: Design and evaluation of children's education interactive learning system based on human computer interaction technology.
citation: Li Mengru, Lv Yang, Pu Yongming, Wu Min. (2025). Design and evaluation of children’s education interactive learning system based on human computer interaction technology. Scientific Reports 15, 6135. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-90800-y
title: Immediate multimodal feedback on every child interaction in a learning system
description: A lesson-level interaction design in which the system responds to each child operation with immediate, clear feedback delivered through multiple modalities. The article states that "the system incorporates a feedback mechanism that provides immediate and clear responses to each user's operation", encompassing sound prompts, visual animations or vibrations, so children understand their actions were recognized. For example, completing a drag-and-drop jigsaw action triggers a success sound and a green checkmark.
requirements: Event-driven interaction mode capturing and processing every user action in real time
Intuitive operation suited to children's cognitive and operational abilities
target_learning_goals: understanding that actions are recognized and executed
sustained engagement with learning tasks
examples: When a child completes a drag-and-drop action in a jigsaw puzzle, the system emits a success sound signal and displays a green checkmark.

article_title: Virtual reality or personal computer-based gynecologic pelvic exam simulation: medical student preferences.
citation: Plotzker Rosalyn E., Harmon Derek J., Kanellitsas Tim, Klein Barbie A. (2025). Virtual reality or personal computer-based gynecologic pelvic exam simulation: medical student preferences. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-06757-z
title: Immersive learning as reinforcement of cognitive learning through physically experiencing a procedure (embodied cognition)
description: The article advances an account in which immersive learning — "in which a user physically experiences the procedure" — may reinforce cognitive learning and also address the embodied aspects of the exam, since gaining proficiency in physical exam skills requires simulation and motor learning beyond factual recall. Participants emphasized the value of physically turning their body or reaching for instruments, and the authors connect this to embodied cognition and body pedagogics. VR is described as a responsive platform for gamification elements such as appropriate challenge, active engagement with minimum guidance, and engaging formats that raise motivation.
requirements: an immersive modality in which the user physically performs procedure movements within a responsive environment
constraints: the account is presented as the authors' interpretation of participant emphasis on physicality and movement, not a tested mechanism in this study
target_learners: preclinical medical students learning procedural physical exam skills
target_learning_goals: motor learning and spatial orientation for physical exams
reinforcement of cognitive learning about exam steps
examples: Participants demonstrated the physical movements as they spoke during their discussion, and one described being made to think more spatially about how to perform the exam

title: Improve veterinary students' academic fit by understanding their interests and needs
description: The article recommends that educators and curriculum designers attend to how well courses match students' interests and needs, because fit predicts well-being and, via engagement, performance. As printed: "Veterinary educators and curriculum planners should pay more attention to improving the academic fit of veterinary students by understanding their interests and needs better since it is the best predictor of students' well-being". The recommendation rests on the study's SEM findings.
requirements: Knowledge of students' interests and needs, e.g. through feedback or survey instruments
constraints: Evidence base is a cross-sectional self-report study, so causal benefits of fit adjustments are not established
target_learning_goals: academic engagement
well-being and exhaustion reduction
academic performance
examples: The authors suggest teachers can reduce exhaustion through academic fit adjustment, noting "the better the academic fit of veterinary students, the less likely they are going to become exhausted"

article_title: Development and feasibility of an oral health e-learning program for long-term Japanese overseas workers: a pilot randomized controlled trial.
citation: Sasayama Kiriko, Momoi Yasuko, Gilmour Stuart, Ota Erika. (2023). Development and feasibility of an oral health e-learning program for long-term Japanese overseas workers: a pilot randomized controlled trial. BMC Oral Health. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12903-023-03361-9
title: Information-motivation-behavioural skills (IMB) model as the framework for designing an oral health self-care behaviour-change intervention
description: The article uses the information-motivation-behavioural skills (IMB) model as the psychological framework for its e-learning program, stating that "Interventions to improve oral health-related behaviours need to be designed based on a psychological model or theory." The model "identifies information as 'the initial prerequisite for performing health behaviours', two factors of motivation governing beliefs about a particular health behaviour and perceived social support, and dimensions of behavioural skills and self-efficacy required to implement behavioural change." The program's five chapters and its outcome measures (knowledge, motivation, self-efficacy) were structured around these IMB components.
requirements: Interventions to improve oral health-related behaviours should be designed based on a psychological model or theory, as the article states
target_learners: adult overseas workers aged 20-44 preparing for long-term stays in low- and middle-income countries
target_learning_goals: oral health self-care knowledge
motivation for oral health behaviour
oral care self-efficacy and self-care behaviours such as fluoride toothpaste use
examples: The e-learning program comprised five chapters structured to convey information, build motivation via cartoons based on interviews with people who have stayed abroad, and develop self-efficacy through a self-check list, practical care guidance and a comprehension quiz.

article_title: Development and feasibility of an oral health e-learning program for long-term Japanese overseas workers: a pilot randomized controlled trial.
citation: Sasayama Kiriko, Momoi Yasuko, Gilmour Stuart, Ota Erika. (2023). Development and feasibility of an oral health e-learning program for long-term Japanese overseas workers: a pilot randomized controlled trial. BMC Oral Health. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12903-023-03361-9
title: IMB-based e-learning design pattern: cartoons, videos, self-check lists and interactive quizzes organised in five chapters
description: The program's instructional design combined several media and interaction formats to deliver an IMB-based intervention: it "provided informed evidence in an interactive, interesting, and easy-to-understand way using cartoons, videos, and interactive quizzes." Cartoons "were developed based on interviews with people who have stayed abroad," a second chapter provided a self-check list of risk factors, and a final chapter contained a test of understanding. Participants' evaluations indicated the illustrations and cartoons were highly appreciated.
requirements: Content should be kept easy to understand and engaging, using media (cartoons, videos, quizzes) matched to the target behaviour-change constructs
constraints: The article reports one negative comment that it took too much time to learn the material, and the authors judge the content needs to be reduced slightly
target_learners: adult overseas workers aged 20-44 preparing for long-term assignments abroad
target_learning_goals: understanding oral diseases and evidence-based prevention
adopting fluoride toothpaste use and self-care behaviours
examples: The five-chapter program ran on the cloud-based EDEN LMS and included a knowledge chapter, a self-check list, practical prevention content, pre-travel oral care guidance and a final comprehension quiz.

article_title: Evaluation of IMproving Palliative care Education and Training Using Simulation in Dementia (IMPETUS-D) a staff simulation training intervention to improve palliative care of people with advanced dementia living in nursing homes: a cluster randomised controlled trial.
citation: Tropea Joanne, Nestel Debra, Johnson Christina, Hayes Barbara J., Hutchinson Anastasia F., Brand Caroline, Le Brian H., Blackberry Irene, Caplan Gideon A., Bicknell Ross, Hepworth Graham, Lim Wen K. (2022). Evaluation of IMproving Palliative care Education and Training Using Simulation in Dementia (IMPETUS-D) a staff simulation training intervention to improve palliative care of people with advanced dementia living in nursing homes: a cluster randomised controlled trial. BMC Geriatrics. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12877-022-02809-x
title: IMPETUS-D: an 11-module screen-based simulation training program on dementia-specific palliative care for nursing home staff
description: IMPETUS-D is an online simulation training program developed for the study by experts in simulation and healthcare worker education. "The program comprised 11 modules covering key aspects of best practice palliative and end-of-life care for people with dementia living in nursing homes", with case studies and short video scenarios filmed in authentic care home settings used as the basis for questions to practise 'what to say' in different situations. Modules ranged from 15 to 45 minutes; PCWs were expected to complete five core modules and nurses the goals-of-care and communication modules, with payment of three hours' salary as an incentive. It was evaluated in the cluster RCT reported here.
requirements: Access to a learning management system delivering the modules on desktop, laptop, tablet, or smartphone
Staff time to complete assigned core modules, supported by incentives such as paid training time
constraints: Its voluntary nature, complexity with multiple modules, targeting multiple disciplines, and use of a separate LMS were reported as barriers to implementation
target_learners: Personal care workers in nursing homes
target_learning_goals: Dementia-specific palliative and end-of-life care knowledge and skills
Goals-of-care planning and communication with residents and families
Recognising and managing symptoms at the end of life
examples: The modules used short video scenarios filmed in authentic care home settings, for example practising what to say when family are worried about a resident not eating towards the end of life.
